subject: POC observability plan & success criteria - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fintechx.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Recap + proposed observability plan for POC

Hi Alex — great chat this morning. Thanks for walking through FintechX's goals for the POC. Below is a concise recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before we kick off.

Recap (what we heard)
- Objective: validate Redwood inference for <100ms median tail latency on core risk-scoring model and measure cost/throughput at 10k requests/day.
- Success criteria: latency SLO (median < 80ms, p95 < 200ms), inference cost per 1M tokens < target we discussed, and model output parity on 100 held-out prompts (>= 95% pass rate per FintechX eval).
- Security/compliance: FintechX needs audit logs, per-request tracing IDs, and the ability to export logs and metrics to your Splunk instance.

Proposed observability plan for the POC (short version)
- Dashboards: prebuilt Grafana dashboard (latency distribution, token throughput, error rate, queue depth). We’ll share a mock.
- Tracing: automatic request IDs propagated through the service; spans for routing, model select, and decode.
- Logs: structured access/error logs (JSON) with fields: request_id, model_version, latency_ms, tokens_in/out, user_id (hashed). Export via S3 + forwarder to Splunk for FintechX.
- Metrics to monitor: requests/s, tokens/s, median/p95 latency, decode time, KV cache hit rate, queue depth, model fallback count, gRPC timeouts. Alerting thresholds: p95 latency > 250ms for 5m, error rate > 1% 10m.
- Ownership: Redwood will provision dashboards and a runbook; FintechX to verify ingestion to Splunk and share any additional required log fields.

Attachments: I’ve attached a draft success criteria spreadsheet and the observability runbook mock.

Next steps / timeline
1) FintechX confirms success criteria and security point-of-contact (by EOD 2026-08-04).
2) Redwood will deploy a dedicated POC environment and share Grafana mock + runbook (by 2026-08-07).
3) Joint smoke test + Splunk ingestion test (scheduled week of 2026-08-10).
4) 2-week evaluation window, milestone review on 2026-08-24.

Can you confirm the security contact and whether S3 -> Splunk is acceptable?

Thanks — happy to adjust anything.

—
Marissa Cole

Alex — thanks for the quick reply and for looping in security. A couple concrete answers: 

Evaluation harness
- We'll run the same test harness we use internally for POCs. It supports: 
  * deterministic prompts (seeded sampling) for parity checks
  * full request/response recording so both sides can reproduce outputs
  * evaluation metrics: exact-match/semantic similarity and pass/fail per prompt as you requested.
- Deliverable: a reproducible test bundle (script + prompt set + scoring) that you can run in your environment. We’ll include instructions and Docker image hash for reproducibility.

Log schema (sample fields)
- request_id (uuid)
- timestamp
- model_version
- latency_ms
- decode_time_ms
- tokens_in
- tokens_out
- kv_cache_hit (bool)
- user_id_hashed
- error_code (nullable)

We’ll attach a small sample JSON file for your ETL team. For S3 -> Splunk ingestion we recommend a daily partitioned prefix and a small manifest file.

Observability deliverables (what Redwood will provide)
- Grafana dashboard JSON + hosted preview (read-only)
- Tracing spans in OpenTelemetry format and a sample trace for the smoke test
- Structured log samples and an S3 export setup guide
- Runbook with troubleshooting steps and escalation path

Ownership and single points of contact
- Redwood: Marissa (POC lead, runbook/dashboards), Jordan (ops, deployment and smoke tests), Aditya (profiling and kernel selection support)
- FintechX: Alex (ML lead), Priya (product), FintechX Security alias (evidence/ingestion)

I’ve attached the runbook and a dashboard mock. If this looks good I’ll schedule the environment provision for Friday 8/07 and propose smoke-test slots for 8/10–8/12.
